$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-REHAB-004 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §10.7 and the RF-REHAB-004 inventory entry. Clinical-content-only PROHIBITION rule: cites evidence claims and has NO architecture references (architecture_refs intentionally empty per v1.2 §4.3). Expresses the prohibition against universal RF dosage / universal prescription only: the RF module must not invent universal set counts, repetition counts, intensity, rest, weekly frequency, or progression increments, and any active universal RF dose without a separately approved source and version must fail content validation. QRF-022 and QRF-035 are research-gap claims that block universal RF dosing, not prescription authority. No dosage, exercise selection, complete plan, RTT, or RTS logic; safety precedence preserved; does not bypass RF-REHAB-001/002/003 or override RF-SAF-006/RF-DX-008/RF-SEV-004/RF-SEV-005. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.

input_contract.$comment: The prohibition scope taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §10.7. No universal RF prescription or dose may be invented; the enumerated universal parameters are recorded only to mark what is prohibited.

decision_contract.$comment: Universal-dosage prohibition structure only. No universal RF prescription/dose may be active rule logic; any active universal RF dose without a separately approved source and version must fail content validation. QRF-022/QRF-035 are research-gap claims, not prescription authority. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Clinical_content normative source; normative strength PROHIBITION; permitted_use prohibited_autonomous_rule. Architecture references are intentionally empty: per v1.2 §4.3 clinical-content rules cite valid evidence_claim_ids and do not carry architecture refs (none in §10.7); [] means 'none in source', not 'missing'. Evidence grades/roles preserved per source: QRF-022 (I1) and QRF-035 (I1) are RF-dosage research-gap claims that BLOCK universal RF dosing and must not be generalized into a universal RF prescription, exercise dose, loading rule, progression rule, phase prescription, or return rule. Per §10.7 behavior preserved exactly: the RF module must not invent universal sets, repetitions, intensity, rest, weekly frequency, or progression increments. Per §10.7 engineering consequence preserved exactly: any active universal RF dose without a separately approved source and version must fail content validation (captured as content_validation_requirement, aligning with v1.2 §17 case 28 where universal RF sets/repetitions/frequency without an approved dosage source fails CI). The rule creates no dosage, selects no exercises or complete exercise plan, generates no complete rehab plan, and produces no return-to-training or return-to-sport decision. Safety-state choice (read §10.7 exactly): §10.7 does NOT assign a closed V3.1 safety state, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty, and the universal-dosage prohibition is represented in decision_contract; no safety state was inferred by analogy. The rule does not bypass the RF-REHAB-001 prescription-input gate, the RF-REHAB-002 loading-dimension constraints, or the RF-REHAB-003 position-tag limits, and does not override RF-SAF-006, RF-DX-008, RF-SEV-004, or RF-SEV-005; uncertainty is preserved when source quality is weak, exercise metadata is incomplete, prescription inputs are incomplete, or loading tolerance cannot be safely determined. Rehabilitation prohibition rule, not a safety rule. No rehab prescription engine is authored here (deferred to the later rehab selection and planning objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
